items.title: Red Holloway interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: Now Bird was one who could play, I mean, fast and he could play a whole lot of stuff

ctx.x: And there seems to be a difference there, I’d like you to speak on this. The difference between execution and expression.

Well there were a few people who could execute and express themselves beautifully and make it sound very melodic and convincing and with feeling. Then you’ve got some who play four million notes and you don’t feel nothing and you haven’t heard anything, you know. Now Bird was one who could play, I mean, fast and he could play a whole lot of stuff, and Sonny Stitt, Diz, and I mean with feeling, like when Bird played with Jay McShann. Man that cat when he got through playing some of them solos he played a million…
express themselves musically. So it’s possible to play a lot of different things and still play it with feeling.
